messages:
Maria: Thanks everyone for the runtime deep-dive earlier. Quick thread to capture unanswered Qs and action items — I'll paste the list and call on folks. If you were on the call and want to add anything, reply here.

Jules: TL;DR of kernel/ batching roadmap from the meeting: 1) short-term: perf-critical kernel hotfixes (Q2) 2) mid-term: continuous batching rework + dynamic kernel selector (Q3) 3) long-term: compiler-backed fused kernels + quantization-aware planning (Q4)

Sam: Can you clarify what "continuous batching rework" means for tail latency? Are we expecting higher p95 for small requests?

Jules: @Sam short answer: no, goal is same or better p95. We're shifting to dynamic batch sizing + predictive flush so small requests are rarely batched unless latency budget allows. We'll add unit tests for p95 regressions.

Ethan: For dedicated customers — how will this interact with autoscaling? Any risk of sudden batch flushes causing spikes?

Ravi: Autoscaler will be updated to be batch-aware. Policy will look at queue depth + predicted batch sizes. Plan: soft-scale earlier to avoid mass flush.

Kara: On KV cache eviction — current LRU evicts too aggressively under long contexts. Any plan?

Jules: Yes. Prototype: segmented LRU + prefix pinning. We're rolling an experiment on a subset of traffic next week. Expect config: `kv_cache.segmented=true ; kv_cache.pin_prefixes=[\"/system\", \"/user/pm\"]`

Priya: Who owns the experiment and how do customers opt in?

Sam: Experiment run by eng-runtime + eng-ml. Customers can opt in via rollout flag in console (route-level setting) or we'll auto-run on low-risk routes.

Maria: Action item: @Jules share the experiment doc + perf baseline by Tue EOD. @Ravi draft autoscaler heuristics PR by end of week. @Sam coordinate eval prompts for p95 tests.

Jules: Uploading experiment doc: https://redwood.internal/docs/runtime/kv-seg-lru (internal), recording clipped to section.

meeting-bot: Recording and slides uploaded: https://meetings.redwood.ai/rec/1789456789

Kara: small ask — can we expose a `batch_size_hint` at the SDK level so product teams can opt for lower latency at cost?

Ravi: yes, on the roadmap. We'll add `batch_hint` to SDK v0.9 with server-side enforcement (max override permitted).

Sam: quick note on quantization: are we shipping INT8 support before fused kernels?

Jules: We're landing low-risk quant sim in Q3; production INT8 (with validation harness + kernel support) targeted Q4. Q4 will be gated on eval stability.

Priya: Are there any customer-facing breaking changes or need to notify dedicated customers?

Maria: We'll notify Dedicated customers before each major rollout and offer canary windows. Non-breaking by default.

Kara: :thumbsup:

Sam: Thanks, that helps. I'll add 10 eval prompts to the shared doc.

Maria: Closing notes: if you need follow-ups, ping me or @Jules. Will post minutes later. :v:
